thought:
The user wants me to review a Windows-native acceptance harness against a backend API. They explicitly say:
{
  "verdict": "changes-required",
  "findings": [
    "Windows sharing semantics not fully validated: harness assumes FILE_SHARE_READ|WRITE|DELETE but backend may reject DELETE on open handles; test will falsely pass.",
    "No-clobber/replace byte and identity assertions lack explicit ACL check before 0-byte write; backend could reject due to inherited private-root binding.",
    "Cleanup/owned handle lifetime not asserted: finally block assumes rig=None but no test verifies handle close before receipt write.",
    "Inherited-file private-root binding not exercised: no test creates file under private root and verifies ACL mutation refusal.",
    " - Receipt write after status logic creates race if write fails on non-Windows exit2 path.",
    "Module no-fallback guarantee incomplete: no test for load failure after is_file/is_symlink check; backend import side effects (ctypes) not isolated.",
    "Unsupported non-Windows exit2 truthful but receipt[' cleanup'] misleading when nothing created."
  ],
  "coverage_limits": [
    "Windows tests not executed; harness proves only leaf primitives.",
    "Ancestor pinning and full portable protocol out of scope.",
    "Backend defects reported only if they invalidate harness primitives.

findings.issue: Hard-link restoration false-fails. alias.unlink() runs while rig.file()'s handle is still open. File opens use share mode 1 (FILE_SHARE_READ) and never FILE_SHARE_DELETE, and this open is not renameable, so DeleteFile on the alias gets a sharing violation. The links==1 and same-identity asserts after the finally are unreachable, so the suite cannot pass. Source-only; not executed.
findings.fix: Keep the open handle only for the multi-link open/snapshot refusals and the byte check. Close it, then unlink the alias, then reopen and require links==1, the same volume serial and file index, and BEFORE. Unlink only if the alias exists so a failed os.link is not replaced by FileNotFoundError.

findings.issue: Junction non-follow can false-pass. refuses() treats every NativeError as success and drops code. Opening with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT fails in snapshot as unsafe-storage because the leaf has FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT. Removing that flag follows the junction, then snapshot raises conflict because final_path is the target. Bytes stay intact, so the check still passes. Source-only; not executed.
findings.fix: Catch NativeError on the junction open and require code unsafe-storage. conflict means the target was followed. Keep the preserved-byte check and rmdir of the junction only.

findings.issue: Inherited-child binding is only half-tested. Refusal without a root and success with rig.root_handle do not prove the root must contain the child. A backend that accepts any private directory and skips the ancestor/prefix check still passes, with SDDL and bytes unchanged.
findings.fix: Add a second private directory that does not contain the child. verify_private(child, private_root=that handle) must raise NativeError. Re-read SDDL and bytes so the refusal did not repair anything. Keep the no-root refusal and the real-root admission.

findings.issue: Receipt status is untruthful when a check fails and cleanup also fails. finally always replaces status with cleanup-failed, so a real assertion failure (active_check and failure still set) is reported as cleanup-failed. passed stays false, but the primary status is wrong.
findings.fix: If status is already failed, keep it and only record handles_drained/cleanup false. Set cleanup-failed only when the checks had otherwise passed.

coverage_limits: Source review only; this harness was not executed on Windows. Hard-link sharing and junction follow-versus-conflict are inferred from the supplied open flags, snapshot order, and Win32 share rules.
Leaf primitives only. Ancestor pinning and ancestor-junction refusal are explicitly out of scope and are not missing tests. A pass would not admit the backend or lift production Windows holds.
Selected-module no-fallback and non-Windows exit 2 (no import, no fixture, passed false) match the source and were not run.

Win32Native.delete is not exercised. No-clobber publication and post-sharing replace re-check same-handle bytes/identity before close; only the dedicated replacement check re-opens the destination and compares file index. Sharing denial correctly accepts any NativeError (backend maps Win32 32 to unavailable, not conflict).
